trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.evening: Arrive at El Prat Airport at 19:20. Take the L9 Sud metro line to Torrassa, then transfer to reach Sant Just Desvern area (~45-60 min, ~€5.15 with T-Casual card). Check in to Sercotel Porta Barcelona, freshen up, then take a short stroll around the local neighbourhood to get oriented. Head to a nearby bar for a welcome cerveza and pintxos to unwind after the flight.

meals.lunch: N/A - on the plane or airport
meals.dinner: Bar/restaurant near the hotel in Sant Just Desvern — look for a local 'menú del día' spot or a neighbourhood tapas bar. Budget ~€10-14 for a beer, bread, and a plate of patatas bravas or bocadillo.

day_by_day.notes: Buy a T-Casual 10-trip metro card at the airport (€11.35) — it will save money throughout the trip. August in Barcelona averages 28.9°C so pack light clothes. Keep valuables secure on the metro.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro into central Barcelona (use T-Casual card). Start the day with the Sagrada Família Guided Tour — book skip-the-line tickets in advance online (~€26-33 with tower access). Arrive early around 9:00-9:30 AM before the heat peaks. The guided tour lasts ~1.5 hours and covers Gaudí's architectural genius, the Nativity and Passion facades, and the stunning interior forest of columns.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take the metro to the Gothic Quarter for the Gothic Quarter Walking Tour (~€15-20 for a guided group tour, or self-guided for free). Explore the Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, Roman ruins of Barcino, and the narrow medieval lanes. Duck into shaded alleyways to escape the afternoon heat. Visit the free Pont del Bisbe bridge and the Plaça de Sant Jaume.
day_by_day.evening: As the sun sets, the Gothic Quarter comes alive. Grab a pre-dinner drink at one of the terrace bars on Plaça Reial (~€3-5 for a beer). Then explore El Born neighbourhood nearby for its vibrant bar scene. Check out Bar del Pla or similar local spots. This is a great intro to Barcelona's nightlife — bars fill up after 10 PM and the energy builds toward midnight.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and croissant or tostada con tomate at a local café near the hotel or near Sagrada Família — budget ~€3-5.
meals.lunch: La Boqueria Market Food Experience on La Rambla (~€10-15) — sample fresh tapas, jamón ibérico, olives, and local cheeses at market stalls. Arrive by 1 PM before it gets too crowded.
meals.dinner: El Born area — look for a set menú del día (available until ~4 PM) or evening tapas. Try Bar Celta Pulpería for affordable pulpo and tapas (~€12-16 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Sagrada Família tickets sell out weeks in advance in August — book online before the trip. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Gothic Quarter cobblestones. Stay hydrated; carry a refillable water bottle (public fountains are available throughout the city).

day_by_day.morning: Head to Park Güell (free to walk the lower park; ~€10 for the Monumental Zone — book online). Arrive at 9:00 AM to beat the crowds and the heat. Admire Gaudí's mosaic terraces, the famous dragon staircase, and panoramic views over Barcelona. Spend 1.5-2 hours exploring the park's architectural wonders and lush gardens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk downhill from Park Güell through the Gràcia neighbourhood — one of Barcelona's most charming and local-feeling districts. Browse the boutiques and street art, visit Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia. Then make your way to Casa Batlló or Casa Milà (La Pedrera) on Passeig de Gràcia — admire the exteriors for free (interior entry is €25-35, optional if budget allows). The entire Manzana de la Discordia block has three stunning modernista buildings to photograph.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Eixample district for Barcelona's famous LGBTQ+ and design-bar nightlife scene (the 'Gayxample' area). Alternatively, head back to El Born or Barceloneta beach area for sunset drinks. The beach bars (chiringuitos) are lively and affordable. After midnight, explore clubs like Sala Apolo or Razzmatazz (entry ~€12-18, often includes a drink) for Barcelona's legendary nightlife.

meals.breakfast: Pick up a fresh pastry and café amb llet at a bakery in Gràcia neighbourhood (~€3-4).
meals.lunch: Grab a bocadillo or fresh fruit from a local supermarket (Mercadona or Lidl) near Gràcia for a budget picnic in the park (~€5-7).
meals.dinner: Eixample neighbourhood — try Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca for excellent tapas at reasonable prices (~€15-20). Arrive before 9 PM to avoid a long queue.

day_by_day.notes: Park Güell Monumental Zone tickets must be booked online in advance. The walk from Park Güell to Gràcia is downhill and very pleasant in the morning. If clubbing, note that Barcelona clubs typically don't fill up until 1-2 AM — pace yourself!

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro to Barceloneta and spend the morning at the beach. Arrive by 9:00-10:00 AM to claim a good spot before it gets packed (Barcelona beaches are very crowded in August). Swim in the Mediterranean, relax, and enjoy the sea breeze. Walk along the Passeig Marítim promenade and admire Frank Gehry's golden 'Fish' sculpture near the W Hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the El Raval neighbourhood — visit the MACBA (Museu d'Art Contemporani de Barcelona) exterior plaza, a hub for skaters and street culture. Walk through the colourful streets of El Raval and visit the Mercat de Sant Antoni (a beautifully restored 19th-century market) for browsing and a cool respite. Check out the Palau Güell (another Gaudí masterpiece, entry ~€12) if budget allows — it's less crowded than other Gaudí sites.
day_by_day.evening: El Raval and Parallel avenue come alive at night. Head to Bar Marsella (one of Barcelona's oldest bars, est. 1820) in El Raval for a historic absinthe experience (~€5-7 per drink). Then explore the Parallel area for live music venues and theatre bars. For a bigger night out, Sala Apolo on Avinguda del Paral·lel hosts excellent club nights (~€12-15 entry).

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at a beach-side café in Barceloneta — tostada con tomate y jamón and a coffee (~€5-7).
meals.lunch: Barceloneta has many affordable chiringuitos and takeaway spots. Try a fresh bocadillo de calamares or a portion of paella from a local spot (~€8-12). Avoid the most touristy restaurants right on the beach for better value.
meals.dinner: El Raval — try Elisabets restaurant on Carrer d'Elisabets for a classic, cheap Catalan menú del día (~€10-13 for three courses with wine). Very popular with locals.

day_by_day.notes: Barceloneta beach gets extremely crowded in August — go early. Watch out for pickpockets on the beach and La Rambla. Apply high-SPF sunscreen. Bar Marsella is cash only and keeps irregular hours — check before going.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Montjuïc cable car or funicular (included with T-Casual card for funicular) up to Montjuïc hill. Visit the Castell de Montjuïc (entry ~€5) for sweeping panoramic views over Barcelona, the port, and the Mediterranean. Explore the castle's ramparts and gardens. Walk through the beautiful Jardins de Laribal and Jardí Botànic area (free or ~€3.50 entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head down to the Poble Sec neighbourhood at the foot of Montjuïc — one of Barcelona's most up-and-coming and affordable areas. Browse the Carrer de Blai, famous for its pintxos bars where you can eat well for very little. Visit the Pavelló Mies van der Rohe (Barcelona Pavilion, ~€7) — a masterpiece of modernist architecture and a must for architecture lovers. Then stroll through the Eixample one last time to admire the grid layout and modernista buildings.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Barcelona — return to the Gothic Quarter or El Born for a farewell tapas crawl. Visit 3-4 bars and order one or two small dishes at each (patatas bravas, croquetas, pan con tomate). End the night with a walk along La Rambla (stay alert for pickpockets) and a final drink at a rooftop bar if budget allows. Head back to the hotel and pack for departure.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and a croissant or magdalenas from a local bakery or supermarket near the hotel (~€3-4).
meals.lunch: Carrer de Blai pintxos bars in Poble Sec — load up on pintxos at €1-2 each. Budget ~€8-12 for a very satisfying lunch with a drink.
meals.dinner: Gothic Quarter tapas crawl — budget ~€15-20 total across several bars. Try El Xampanyet in El Born for cava and anchovies, or Bar Cañete near El Raval for excellent traditional tapas.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed for a late departure. The T-Casual card should have enough trips remaining for the return journey. Consider buying some local products (olive oil, canned seafood, turron) at a supermarket as affordable souvenirs. August 15 is Assumption Day — some smaller shops may still have reduced hours on nearby dates.

day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Barcelona El Prat Airport at 19:20. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the Aerobus or metro L9 Sud to Sant Just Desvern. Check in to Sercotel Porta Barcelona, freshen up, and take a relaxed evening stroll around the local neighbourhood to get your bearings.

meals.breakfast: N/A – on board or at airport
meals.dinner: Casual dinner near the hotel – try La Taberna de Sant Just or a neighbourhood tapas bar in Sant Just Desvern for patatas bravas, croquetas, and a glass of house wine. Budget ~€20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. The journey from the airport to Sant Just Desvern takes roughly 30–45 minutes. Confirm your hotel's check-in process in advance. Avoid scheduling anything in the city centre tonight – rest is key for the days ahead. August evenings are warm (~24°C), so light clothing is fine.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour – Take the metro from Sant Just Desvern (FGC line) into central Barcelona and head to Gaudí's iconic unfinished basilica. Book a skip-the-line guided tour (pre-booked online) for a 9:00–10:30 AM slot to beat the midday heat and crowds. Marvel at the Nativity and Passion facades, the soaring interior columns, and the stained-glass light show. Optionally add tower access for panoramic city views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Park Güell & Gràcia Neighbourhood Exploration – After a light lunch in Gràcia, head uphill to Park Güell (timed entry ticket required). Explore the mosaic terraces, gingerbread gatehouses, and the Hypostyle Room. Stroll back down through the charming Gràcia neighbourhood, browsing its boutiques and leafy plazas like Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia.
day_by_day.evening: Barceloneta Beach & El Born Nightlife Circuit – Head to Barceloneta Beach for a golden-hour sunset stroll along the Mediterranean shore. Then move into the trendy El Born district for dinner and drinks. Explore Bar del Pla or El Xampanyet for vermouth and pintxos, then bar-hop through El Born's atmospheric medieval lanes.

meals.breakfast: Café and croissant at a local bakery near the hotel or grab a coffee at a café near Sagrada Família before the tour. Budget ~€5–8.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Gràcia – try La Pepita or a neighbourhood menú del día (set lunch menu with starter, main, dessert, and drink) for ~€12–15 per person.
meals.dinner: El Born tapas dinner at Bar del Pla or Llamber – shared plates of croquetas, anchovies, and grilled vegetables with local craft beer or cava. Budget ~€25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: August heat peaks around 29°C in the afternoon – wear sunscreen and carry water, especially at Park Güell which has limited shade. Book Sagrada Família and Park Güell tickets well in advance online. The El Born nightlife scene picks up after 22:00 – pace yourself for the week ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Gothic Quarter Walking Tour – Start early (9:00 AM) to explore Barcelona's medieval Gothic Quarter before the heat and tourist crowds build. Join a guided walking tour through Roman ruins, the Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, and the narrow labyrinthine lanes of the Barri Gòtic. Discover hidden courtyards and centuries of layered history on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: La Boqueria Market Food Experience – Walk up La Rambla to the legendary Mercat de la Boqueria. Sample fresh tapas, jamón ibérico, local cheeses, seafood, and tropical fruits from the market stalls. Browse the vibrant colours and aromas of one of Europe's most famous public markets. Afterwards, explore the El Raval neighbourhood nearby or rest at a shaded café terrace.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop bar experience in the Eixample district – Head to a rooftop bar such as the one at Hotel Pulitzer or La Isabela Rooftop for cocktails with skyline views as the sun sets. Then enjoy a relaxed dinner in the Eixample, Barcelona's elegant modernist grid neighbourhood, before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at a café in the Gothic Quarter before the tour starts – try Cafè de l'Acadèmia area for a coffee and toast with tomato (pa amb tomàquet). Budget ~€6–10.
meals.lunch: La Boqueria market lunch – graze on market tapas, fresh seafood at a market bar stool, and seasonal fruit. Budget ~€15–20 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Eixample – try Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca for excellent tapas and montaditos in a lively mid-range setting. Budget ~€25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: La Boqueria is closed on Sundays. August 18 is a Monday, so it will be open. Arrive at the market before noon to avoid the worst of the tourist rush and get the best selection. The Gothic Quarter tour is best done on foot in comfortable shoes – cobblestones can be uneven. Stay hydrated throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Palau de la Música Catalana & Sant Pere Neighbourhood – Visit the UNESCO-listed Palau de la Música Catalana, Lluís Domènech i Montaner's breathtaking modernista concert hall. Take a guided tour of the interior (book in advance) to see the extraordinary stained-glass skylight and ornate facade. Afterwards, wander the quiet Sant Pere neighbourhood and visit the Santa Caterina Market for a mid-morning coffee.
day_by_day.afternoon: Casa Batlló or Casa Milà (La Pedrera) – Dedicate the afternoon to another Gaudí masterpiece on the Passeig de Gràcia. Choose between Casa Batlló (more theatrical interior) or Casa Milà/La Pedrera (iconic rooftop terrace with warrior chimneys). Both offer audio guides and rooftop access. The Passeig de Gràcia boulevard itself is a showcase of modernista architecture – spot the 'Block of Discord' featuring buildings by Gaudí, Domènech i Montaner, and Puig i Cadafalch.
day_by_day.evening: Nightlife in Eixample & Poble Sec – Enjoy pre-dinner vermouth (vermut) at Bar Calders or Bodega Sepúlveda in Poble Sec. Have dinner on the lively Carrer de Blai (tapas street) with its famous pintxos bars. Later, explore the Eixample's 'Gayxample' area or rooftop bars for a vibrant Tuesday night out.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a café near the hotel or in Sant Pere – try a traditional Spanish breakfast of tostada con tomate y aceite with café con leche. Budget ~€6–9.
meals.lunch: Lunch near Passeig de Gràcia – try Parking Pizza (casual, quality) or a menú del día at a local restaurant off the main boulevard for ~€13–16 per person.
meals.dinner: Pintxos dinner on Carrer de Blai in Poble Sec – multiple bars offer pintxos from €1.50–2.50 each. Budget ~€15–20 per person for a full spread with drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Book Casa Batlló or La Pedrera tickets online well in advance – they sell out quickly in August. The 'Magic Nights' evening events at La Pedrera rooftop are a special option if available on this date (check their website). Poble Sec is a great alternative to the more touristy El Born for an authentic local evening.

day_by_day.morning: Montjuïc Hill & Pavilion Mies van der Rohe – Take the cable car or metro to Montjuïc for a morning of architecture and views. Visit the Barcelona Pavilion (Pavelló Mies van der Rohe), the iconic 1929 German Pavilion rebuilt in 1986 – a minimalist masterpiece of marble, glass, and water. Stroll through the Jardins de Laribal and enjoy panoramic views over the city and port from the Castell de Montjuïc.
day_by_day.afternoon: Barceloneta & Port Olímpic – Descend from Montjuïc and spend a relaxed final afternoon at Barceloneta Beach. Take a swim in the Mediterranean, rent a sun lounger, or simply walk the promenade. Explore the Port Olímpic marina area and visit Frank Gehry's golden 'Fish' sculpture (Peix d'Or). Browse the waterfront for a final taste of Barcelona's coastal character.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in El Born or La Barceloneta – Celebrate your final evening with a proper sit-down dinner at a mid-range restaurant. Try El Suquet de l'Almirall for excellent seafood and rice dishes near the port, or return to El Born for a final round of cocktails and tapas. End the night with a walk along La Rambla and a nightcap at a terrace bar.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a café near Montjuïc or pack a pastry from a local bakery for the cable car ride up. Budget ~€5–8.
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Barceloneta – try La Cova Fumada (cash only, arrive early) for the original bombas and grilled seafood, or a chiringuito beach bar for paella. Budget ~€20–30 per person.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at El Suquet de l'Almirall or a quality seafood restaurant near the port. Enjoy fideuà (noodle paella), fresh grilled fish, and a bottle of Albariño. Budget ~€35–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Check departure logistics for your return journey before the final evening – confirm airport transfer times from Sant Just Desvern. The Montjuïc cable car (Telefèric de Montjuïc) runs from Paral·lel metro station. La Cova Fumada does not take reservations and closes early when food runs out – arrive by 13:00. August 20 is a Thursday, so the city will be lively for a final night out.

day_by_day.notes: Disfrutar and Tickets require reservations made months in advance — confirm before the trip. The Gothic Quarter is best explored on foot in the morning before the heat peaks. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Architecture Deep Dive — Eixample Modernisme Route: Spend the morning on a self-guided or private-guided tour of Barcelona's Eixample district, the heart of Catalan Modernisme. Visit Casa Batlló (book the premium 'Magic Nights' experience or the standard morning tour with AR glasses) and Casa Milà (La Pedrera), two of Gaudí's most celebrated residential masterpieces. Explore the rooftop of La Pedrera for iconic views of the city's skyline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Montjuïc & Poble Sec Exploration: Take a private car or cable car up to Montjuïc for sweeping panoramic views of Barcelona and the Mediterranean. Visit the Fundació Joan Miró for world-class modern art, and stroll through the Jardins de Laribal. Descend into the Poble Sec neighborhood for a relaxed afternoon exploring its emerging food and arts scene — visit the Sala Apolo area and browse local galleries.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at La Isabela rooftop bar at the Hotel 1898 on La Rambla, followed by a premium dinner in the Eixample. Cap the night with Barcelona's sophisticated cocktail bar scene — visit Paradiso (ranked among the world's best bars, hidden behind a pastrami bar door in El Born) and Two Schmucks for expertly crafted cocktails.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Forn de Sant Jaume on Passeig de Gràcia — an iconic Eixample bakery and café with exquisite pastries and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Bodega 1900 (another Albert Adrià concept) in Poble Sec — a refined, nostalgic take on traditional Spanish vermouth bar culture with elevated tapas
meals.dinner: Dinner at Lasarte — a three-Michelin-star restaurant helmed by Martín Berasategui, offering an extraordinary Basque-Catalan tasting menu in an elegant setting

day_by_day.notes: Casa Batlló and La Pedrera tickets must be pre-booked. The 'Magic Nights' experience at Casa Batlló (evenings) is a spectacular alternative if preferred. Paradiso bar may have a queue — arrive early or ask the hotel concierge to arrange priority access.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely Morning & Luxury Shopping: Start the final full day with a slow, indulgent breakfast. Spend the late morning browsing the luxury boutiques along Passeig de Gràcia — Hermès, Louis Vuitton, Loewe (in a stunning Domènech i Montaner building), and local high-end Catalan designers. Visit the Fundació Antoni Tàpies, housed in a beautiful modernista building, for a cultural finale.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private Sailing Experience on the Mediterranean: Arrange a private luxury catamaran or yacht charter from Port Olímpic or Port Vell. Spend the afternoon sailing along the Barcelona coastline, swimming in the Mediterranean, and enjoying chilled cava and fresh seafood on deck. This is the ultimate premium Barcelona afternoon — the city skyline from the water is unforgettable.
day_by_day.evening: Final Night Celebration — Barcelona's Best: Return to shore for a sunset aperitivo at a waterfront terrace. Enjoy a farewell dinner at a premium restaurant of choice, then experience one final night of Barcelona's legendary nightlife — whether a live flamenco show at Tablao Flamenco Cordobés, a jazz set at Jamboree Jazz Club in Plaça Reial, or a final round at the city's best rooftop bars.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent breakfast at Café Zurich on Plaça de Catalunya or in-hotel breakfast — take your time, it's the last day
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood and cava on the private yacht charter — arrange a catered spread with the charter company in advance
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Enoteca Paco Pérez at Hotel Arts Barcelona — a two-Michelin-star restaurant with stunning port views and an exceptional Mediterranean tasting menu

day_by_day.notes: Book the private yacht charter at least 1–2 weeks in advance through the hotel concierge or a luxury charter service like Sailing BCN or Catamaran Barcelona. August weather is ideal for sailing — warm, sunny, and calm seas. Pack sunscreen and a light layer for the evening sail.
